ni-h-pronoun.en: In /\0/, /ní/ is the copula, and /\3/ is a personal pronoun, which takes h after /ní/.

ni-h-demonstrative.en: In /\0/, /ní/ is the copula, and /\3/ is a demonstrative, which takes h after /ní/.

ce-h-pronoun.en: In /\0/, /\3/ is a personal pronoun, which takes h after /cé/.

ni-h-noun.en: In /\0/, /ní/ is the copula. CO17 10.11.8 lists /\3/ among the nouns that take h after /ní/.

ni-h-adj.en: In /\0/, /ní/ is the copula. CO17 10.12.2 lists /\3/ among the adjectives and adverbs that take h after /ní/.

ni-h-phrase.en: In /\0/, /ní/ is the copula. CO17 gives this set phrase with h on the noun after /ní/.

ordinal-h.en: An ordinal number (/dara/, /tríú/, /ceathrú/ ...) puts h before a noun beginning with a vowel: /an dara heochair/, /an t-ochtú heagrán/. /céad/ is the exception: /an chéad áit/.

na-imperative.en: The negative particle of the imperative is /ná/, and it puts h before a vowel: /ná habair/, /ná himigh/.

art-fem.en: After the article /an/, a feminine noun in the nominative singular is lenited, unless it begins with d, t or s: /an bhean/, /an fhuinneog/.

art-masc-nom.en: After the article /an/, a masculine noun is not lenited in the nominative singular (/an fear/). It is lenited in the genitive singular (/mac an fhir/) and, after some prepositions, in the dative.

art-t-vowel.en: After the article /an/, a masculine noun beginning with a vowel takes /t-/ in the nominative singular (/an t-asal/, /an t-eitleán/), and so do /aon/, /aonú/, /ochtó/, /ochtódú/ and /ochtú/ (/an t-aonú háit déag/, /an t-ochtú cluiche/).

art-t-gen.en: In /\0/, /\3/ is a masculine noun after the article. It takes t in the nominative singular (/an t-asal/, /Cá bhfuair tú an t-airgead?/), but not in the genitive.

art-t-s.en: After the article /an/, s followed by a vowel or by l, n or r takes t where another consonant would be lenited: a feminine noun in the nominative singular (/an tslat/, /an tsreang/) and a masculine noun in the genitive singular (/deireadh an tséasúir/, /eochair an tsiopadóra/).

na-h.en: After the article /na/, h goes before a vowel in the genitive singular of a feminine noun and in the plural: /lár na heitilte/, /na huimhreacha/.

den-don.en: After /den/, /don/ and /sa/, the noun is lenited unless it begins with d, t or s: /den chrann/, /don chuideachta/, /sa pháirc/.

prep-lenition.en: The prepositions /de/, /do/, /faoi/, /ionsar/, /mar/, /ó/, /roimh/, /trí/ and /um/ lenite the noun after them: /de thaisme/, /faoi bhord/, /ó bhéal/, /roimh mhaidin/.

de-do.en: The prepositions /de/ and /do/ lenite the noun after them (/de thaisme/, /do bhuachaillí/), and so does /do/ meaning "your" (/do theach/).

de-do-apostrophe.en: /de/ and /do/ are shortened to /d'/ before a vowel, or before f followed by a vowel: /d'athair Sheáin/, /d'fhoghlaimeoirí Gaeilge/ (but /do Fhrancaigh/).

ar-lenition.en: /ar/ usually lenites the noun after it (/ar bhád/, /ar chlé/), but not in phrases that say where or in what state something is, such as /ar ball/, /ar fáil/, /ar siúl/, /ar meisce/. Check whether this is one of those.

gan-lenition.en: /gan/ lenites a noun that has nothing qualifying it, unless it begins with d, t, s or f: /gan mhoill/, /gan chosaint/. A qualified noun, a definite proper name and a verbal noun are not lenited: /gan pingin rua/, /gan Micheál/, /gan géilleadh/.

le-h.en: /le/, and /go/ meaning "to", put h before a noun beginning with a vowel (/le hÁine/, /go hAlasca/); /le/, /go/ and /chomh/ put h before an adjective or adverb beginning with a vowel (/chomh hard le haon chapall/, /Tá sé go hálainn/).

i-eclipsis.en: The preposition /i/ eclipses the word after it: /i mbaile/, /i bpáirc/. Before a vowel it is written /in/: /in Éirinn/.

in-before-consonant.en: Before a consonant the preposition is /i/, with eclipsis (/i mbaile/). /in/ is written before a vowel, and before /bhur/, /dhá/ and /go leor/, titles, abbreviations, foreign place names that have not been Gaelicised, and years in figures: /in dhá áit/, /in Birmingham/, /in 1998/.

aon-lenition.en: /aon/, and /céad/ meaning "first", lenite the noun after them unless it begins with d, t or s: /aon bhia/, /an chéad bhróg/, but /aon duine/, /an chéad teach/.

poss-plural-eclipsis.en: The possessives /ár/, /bhur/ and /a/ meaning "their" eclipse the noun after them: /ár n-athair/, /bhur bpáistí/.

noun-eclipsis.en: A noun is eclipsed only in certain places: after /i/; after /ár/, /bhur/ and /a/ ("their"); after the numbers /seacht/ to /deich/; after the article in the genitive plural; and after the article and some prepositions in the dative (/ar an gcapall/).

adj-fem.en: An adjective after a feminine singular noun (nominative or dative) is lenited: /bean mhór/, /feoil bhlasta/.

adj-masc-gen.en: An adjective after a masculine noun in the genitive singular is lenited: /mac fir mhóir/, /úinéir an chapaill ghlais/.

adj-slender-plural.en: An adjective after a plural noun ending in a slender consonant is lenited: /fir mhóra/.

adj-number.en: An adjective is lenited after a noun with /dhá/ before it, and after a singular noun with a number from /trí/ to /deich/ before it: /dhá bhó bhána/, /trí bhád mhóra/.

adj-lenition.en: An adjective is lenited after a feminine singular noun (/bean mhór/), after a masculine noun in the genitive singular (/mac fir mhóir/), after a plural noun ending in a slender consonant (/fir mhóra/) and after certain numbers; otherwise it is not.

gen-after-fem.en: In /\0/, /\3/ is an indefinite genitive after a feminine singular noun. It is then usually lenited: /cloch shneachta/, /uirlis cheoil/. CO17 10.2.7 lists the exceptions to this rule, including when the second noun is a person, an animal or other living thing (/súil páiste/), when the first noun is part of the second (/cos cathaoireach/), or when the first noun is an action and the second its object (/forbairt pobail/).

gen-after-plural.en: In /\0/, /\3/ is an indefinite genitive after a plural noun ending in a slender consonant. It is then usually lenited: /dualgais bhreise/, /ceadúnais ghnó/. CO17 10.2.8 lists the exceptions to this rule, including when the second noun is a person, an animal or other living thing (/buidéil páiste/), or when the first noun is part of the second (/cláir báid/).

verb-independent.en: In the past tense, the past habitual and the conditional, the verb is lenited even with no particle before it: /mhol mé/, /shábháil sí/, /théidís/, /chuideodh sé/. (/abair/ is never lenited: /dúirt siad/.)

d-past.en: Where a consonant would be lenited, a verb beginning with a vowel, or with f, takes /d'/ in the past tense, the past habitual and the conditional: /d'ól sé/, /d'fhágamar/, /d'imeoinn/.

verb-after-particle.en: The verb is lenited after /ní/, /níor/, /ar/, /cár/, /dár/, /gur/, /murar/, /nár/ and /sular/: /ní fhaca sé/, /níor fhéad mé/, /sílim gur thuig sé/.

verb-after-a-ma.en: The verb is lenited after the direct relative /a/ and after /má/ and /ó/ ("since"): /an bhean a ghlanfaidh an áit/, /má bhíonn sé ann/.

verb-no-lenition.en: In the present, the future and the imperative, a verb is lenited only after a particle that lenites it, such as /ní/, /má/ or the direct relative /a/.

verb-relative-eclipsis.en: The verb is eclipsed after the indirect relative /a/ and after /nach/: /an bhean a dtagann a páistí ar scoil/, /an fear nach gcuirtear cúram air/.

verb-eclipsis.en: A verb is eclipsed only after the particles that eclipse it: /an/, /cá/, /dá/, /go/, /mura/, /nach/, /sula/ and the indirect relative /a/ (/an mbeidh/, /go bhféadfaidh sé/).

relative-a.en: After the relative particle /a/, the verb is lenited when /a/ is the direct relative (/an bhean a ghlanfaidh an áit/) and eclipsed when it is the indirect relative (/an bhean a dtagann a páistí ar scoil/).

number-eclipsis.en: /seacht/, /ocht/, /naoi/ and /deich/ eclipse the noun after them: /seacht ndícheall/, /ocht gcinn/, /naoi mbliana/, /deich n-eachtra/.

number-lenition.en: In /\0/, the noun follows /dhá/, /trí/, /ceithre/, /cúig/ or /sé/, which lenite the singular noun after them: /dhá chrann/, /trí bhád/, /ceithre bhó/. CO17 9.3.2 lists the nouns with a special form after numbers, which are not lenited: /trí seachtaine/, /ceithre cinn déag/.

vn-a-lenition.en: /a/ before a verbal noun (it stands for /do/) lenites it: /obair a dhéanamh/.

art-masc-gen.en: After the article /an/, a masculine noun in the genitive singular is lenited unless it begins with d, t or s: /mac an fhir/, /geata an choláiste/.

copula-lenition.en: The past and conditional forms of the copula (/ba/, /níor/, /ar/, /nár/, /gur/, /dá mba/ ...) lenite the noun or adjective after them: /Ba dhuine mór é/, /Ba dheas uait é/, /Ar mhaith leat é?/

dative-article.en: After a preposition and the article, a noun in the dative singular is eclipsed (/ar an gcapall/) or, in Córas an tSéimhithe, lenited (/ar an chapall/).

vocative.en: The vocative particle /a/ lenites the noun: /a dhuine chóir/, /a chairde na páirte/. If /a/ here means "her", the noun is not lenited, so check which it is.

possessive-lenition.en: The possessives /mo/, /do/ and /a/ meaning "his" lenite the noun after them: /mo mhac/, /do theach/, /a pheann/.

deag-lenition.en: /déag/ is lenited after a singular noun ending in a vowel, and after /dó/: /trí bhó dhéag/, /cúig lá dhéag/, /a dó dhéag/.

number-h.en: /a/ and /na/ put h before a number beginning with a vowel: /ceacht a haon/, /na hocht gcinn/.

ca-h.en: /cá/ puts h before a noun beginning with a vowel: /cá háit?/, /cá huair/.

art-gen-plural.en: After the article /na/, a noun in the genitive plural is eclipsed: /seolta na mbád beag/, /scoil na gcailíní óga/.

non-standard-form.en: Detected as a non-standard word. It may be an older spelling, a dialect form or a common misspelling. Modern dictionaries would likely give /\1/.

unlikely-sequence.en: The sequence of characters /\1/ is highly unlikely in Irish.

near-miss.en: This word isn't in the app's dictionary. The suggestions are dictionary words that differ from it by one letter: added, left out, changed or swapped.

unknown-word.en: This word isn't in the app's dictionary. It may be misspelled, a foreign word, or a correct word the dictionary doesn't have.

compound-lenition.en: The second part of a compound is lenited (/deargbhuile/, /rósghairdín/), except when d, n, t, l or s meet (/antráth/, /catsúil/).

possible-compound.en: /\0/ may be from /\1/, two dictionary words, so it may be a correct compound.

formed-with-prefix.en: /\0/ may be from /\1/, a prefix and a dictionary word, so it may be correct.

formed-from-root.en: /\0/ follows a regular pattern for forming words, so it may be correct.

rare-word.en: /\0/ is very similar to a common word, so it may be incorrect.

common-incorrect.en: This spelling is in the app's list of common incorrect spellings.

more-usual.en: /\0/ may be a dialect form or an older spelling, or it may be incorrect.

from-non-standard.en: /\0/ may be formed from an older spelling, a dialect form or an incorrect spelling. Modern dictionaries would likely give /\1/.

from-incorrect.en: /\0/ is similar to a common misspelling.

from-common-incorrect.en: /\0/ may be from /\1/, which is a common incorrect spelling of /\2/.

gen-after-noun.en: In /\0/, the second noun may depend on the first, and is then usually in the genitive: /Is cóta mná é/. CO17 3.3 lists where the nominative is used instead: /Bíonn siad ag casadh ceol tíre ar an Aoine/.
